output.brief: Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the service's normal range. The upper edge is 0.48%, based on the previous 26 weeks. Three earlier weeks were higher, and each investigation found no fault. The error-budget burn was 0.82x, well below the 2x paging threshold. Bookings were flat and there were no customer complaints. A recount from the raw load balancer logs matches the dashboard, so the rise is not a counting artefact. The higher error rate on new pods that Dario saw is a cache warm-up effect. It appears in every rollout, including a config-only redeploy, and adds only 10–20 errors. That is far too few to explain the weekly rise. So v4.18 is not shown to be at fault, and I can't say whether the replica move or partner-sync traffic played a part. Recommendation: don't roll back today and don't mute the alerts. Muting would remove the protection that would catch a real problem. Log the week at ops review as normal and apply the standard check to the next week. If next week exceeds 0.48% or the burn-rate page fires, open an incident and look at the replica move, partner-sync timing and the fetchwell bump. I'm fairly confident in this, though I didn't check those three causes directly.
